questions.question: A wire in a shape of a circle of radius 28 cm is bent in the form of a square. What is the difference of their areas? (Take pi = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
**Given :**

Radius of wire is 28 cm. 

**Concept used :**

Area of the circle = π radius²

Area of the square = side × side 

Circumference of the circle = 2π × radius 

Perimeter of square = 4 × side 

**Calculations :**

Circumference of the circle = Perimeter of the square (Length will remain same) 

⇒ 2 π × 28 = Perimeter of square 

Perimeter of square = 8 × 22 

So , 

Side of the square = 44 cm 

Now, 

Area of square = 44 × 44 

⇒ 1936 cm²

Area of the circle = π × 28 × 28 

⇒ 2464 cm²

Difference of the areas = 2464 - 1936 

⇒ 528 cm²

**∴ Option 4 will be the correct answer.**

questions.question: A circular arc makes an angle of 15° at the centre. If the radius of the circular arc is 14 cm, what is the perimeter (correct up to two decimal places) of the sector so formed? (π = 3.14)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The perimeter of a sector is the sum of its arc length (l) and twice its radius (2r).

Arc Length (l) = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr

l = (15° ÷ 360°) × 2 × 3.14 × 14

l = (1 ÷ 24) × 87.92 ≈ 3.66 cm

Perimeter = l + 2r = 3.66 + 2(14) = 3.66 + 28 = 31.66 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 31.66 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5fdd692ae6c7f7e44cdbd7ef0fca777e3cb0c7950019a13d94c96ae827421d48.png] 

**Given:**

Angle of the circular arc (θ) = 15°

Radius of the circular arc (r) = 14 cm

Value of π = 3.14

**Formula Used:**

Length of Arc (l) = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr

Perimeter of a Sector = Length of Arc + 2 × Radius

**Calculations:**

⇒ l = (15 ÷ 360) × 2 × 3.14 × 14

⇒ l = (1 ÷ 24) × 87.92

⇒ l = 87.92 ÷ 24

⇒ l ≈ 3.6633 cm

⇒ Perimeter of the Sector = l + 2r

⇒ Perimeter = 3.6633 + (2 × 14)

⇒ Perimeter = 3.6633 + 28

⇒ Perimeter = 31.6633 cm

⇒ Rounding up to two decimal places, Perimeter = 31.66 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 31.66 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Sector

The area of a sector with central angle θ is given by A = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr². Alternatively, if the arc length l is known, the area can be directly calculated as A = (l × r) ÷ 2.

Length of a Circular Arc

The arc length represents the distance along the curved edge of the circle and is calculated as l = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr.

Perimeter vs Arc Length

Students often confuse the perimeter of a sector with the arc length. The arc length is merely the curved boundary, while the full perimeter of the sector must include the two straight radii boundary lines, establishing the formula: Perimeter = l + 2r.
</p

questions.question: If the area of a rhombus is 70 m² and its height is 5 m, its perimeter is ________.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Area of the rhombus = 70 m²

Height of the rhombus = 5 m

**Formula Used:**

Area of a rhombus = Base × Height

Perimeter of a rhombus = 4 × Side

**Calculation:**

Base = Area / Height

Base = 70 / 5

Base = 14 m

Since all sides of a rhombus are equal, the side is equal to the base.

Side = 14 m

Perimeter = 4 × Side

⇒ Perimeter = 4 × 14

⇒ Perimeter = 56 m

**The perimeter of the rhombus is 56 m.**

questions.question: If the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle is 29 cm and the sum of the other two sides is 41 cm, then the difference between the other two sides is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Hypotenuse of the right-angled triangle = 29 cm

Sum of other two sides = 41 cm

**Concept:**

Pythagoras theorem states that in a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse side is equal to the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

**Calculation:**

Let, the length of one side = x cm

So, the length of another side = (41 - x) cm

According to the concept,

x² + (41 - x)² = 29²

⇒ x2 + 41² - 2 × 41 × x + x2 = 292

⇒ x

questions.question: Parallel sides of a trapezium are 21 cm and 14 cm and its area is 875 cm². What is the distance between parallel sides?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for the **height** (distance) of a **trapezium**:

Height = (2 × **Area**) ÷ (Sum of **parallel sides**)

Height = (2 × 875) ÷ (21 + 14)

Height = 1750 ÷ 35 = 50 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 50 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Parallel side 1 (a) = 21 cm

Parallel side 2 (b) = 14 cm

**Area** of trapezium = 875 cm²

**Formula Used:**

**Area of Trapezium** = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × **Height**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b4e791265545fdf199cfecb2a1a73eeaf89d94fd0ded73e52907696aee49674c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 875 = 1/2 × (21 + 14) × h

⇒ 875 = 1/2 × 35 × h

⇒ 875 = 17.5 × h

⇒ h = 875 ÷ 17.5

⇒ h = 50 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 50 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Trapezium

A **trapezium** is a quadrilateral with at least one pair of **parallel sides**. The **height** is the perpendicular distance between these parallel lines.

Median of a Trapezium

The length of the **median** (the segment connecting the midpoints of the non-parallel sides) is the average of the two bases: Median = (a + b) ÷ 2.

Isosceles Trapezium

In an **isosceles trapezium**, the non-parallel sides are equal in length, and the **base angles** are equal.</p

questions.question: The perimeter of a semi circle is 25.7 cm. What is its diameter (in cm)? (π = 3.14)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Perimeter of a semi-circle** = r(π + 2)

Given π = 3.14, Perimeter = r(3.14 + 2) = 5.14r

5.14r = 25.7 ⇒ r = 25.7 ÷ 5.14 = 5 cm

**Diameter** = 2 × r = 2 × 5 = 10 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Perimeter of semi-circle = 25.7 cm, π = 3.14

**Formula Used:** Perimeter = πr + 2r

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/90af99514ee1ed6e680d58b2529239fbe0bf8484aa947cea3f55ffd12941c304.png] 

⇒ r(π + 2) = 25.7

⇒ r(3.14 + 2) = 25.7

⇒ 5.14r = 25.7

⇒ r = 25.7 ÷ 5.14

⇒ r = 5 cm

⇒ **Diameter** = 2r = 2 × 5 = 10 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Semi-circle

The area is half the area of a full circle: Area = (πr²) ÷ 2.

Circle Properties

For a full circle, Circumference = 2πr and Diameter = 2r.

Sector of a Circle

Perimeter of a sector with angle θ = ( θ / 360 ) × 2πr + 2r.</p

questions.question: The area of a square and rectangle are equal. The length of the rectangle is greater than the length of a side of a square by 10 cm and the breadth is less than 5 cm. The perimeter (in cm) of the rectangle is:

questions.question: Original breadth of a rectangular box is 20 cm. The box was then remade in such a way that its length increased by 30% but the breadth decreased by 20% and the area increased by 100 cm². What is the new area of the box?
questions.solution:
**Given****∶**

Original breadth of the rectangular box = b = 20 cm

Percentage increase in length = 30%

Percentage decrease in breadth = 20%

**Calculation****∶**

Let original length of the rectangular box be l.

⇒ Original area of rectangular box = lb = 20l

⇒ Length of the rectangular box after 30% increase = 130/100 × l

⇒ Breadth of the rectangular box after 20% decrease = 80% of b = 80/100 × 20 = 16 cm

⇒ New Area of the rectangular box = 130/100 × l × 16

According to the question,

New Area of the rectangular box = Original area of rectangular box + 100

⇒ 130/100 × l × 16 = 20l + 100

⇒ l(20.8 – 20) = 100

⇒ 0.8l = 100

⇒ l = 1000/8 = 125 cm

∴ New Area of the rectangular box = 130/100 × l × 16 = 130/100 × 125 × 16 = 130 × 20 = 2600 cm²

questions.question: The length of the base of a triangle is 3 cm smaller than the length of its altitude. Its area is 104 cm². What is the length of the base?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The length of the base of a triangle = 3 cm smaller than the length of its altitude

Area of triangle = 104 cm²

**Formula used:**

Area of triangle = 1/2 × base × height

**Calculation:**

Let the length of the base of the triangle be x cm.

The length of the base of a triangle is 3 cm smaller than the length of its altitude = (x + 3)

Now,

Area of triangle = [1/2 × x × (x + 3)] = 104

⇒ (1/2 × x² + 3x) = 104

⇒ x² + 3x = 208

⇒ x² + 3x – 208 = 0

⇒ x² + 16x – 13x – 208 = 0

⇒ x(x + 16) – 13(x + 16) = 0

⇒ (x – 13) (x + 16) = 0

⇒ x = 13, -16

Now,

The length of base of the triangle = x = 13 cm

**∴ The required value is 13 cm**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**Area of triangle = [1/2 × x × (x + 3)] = 104

⇒ x × ( x + 3) = 208

⇒ x × (x + 3) = 13 × 16

⇒ x × (x + 3) = 13 × (13 +3)

On comparing x = 13

The length of base of the triangle = x = 13 cm

∴ The required value is 13 cm

Area of a Semi-Circle

questions.question: Find the area of a rhombus if the perimeter of the rhombus is 52 cm, and one of its diagonals is 10 cm long.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Side** of the **rhombus** (a) = Perimeter ÷ 4 = 52 ÷ 4 = 13 cm.

One **half-diagonal** = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm.

Using **Pythagorean triplet** (5, 12, 13), the other **half-diagonal** is 12 cm.

**Full second diagonal** (d₂) = 12 × 2 = 24 cm.

**Area** = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂ = (1/2) × 10 × 24 = 120 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 120 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Perimeter** of **rhombus** = 52 cm

One **diagonal** (d₁) = 10 cm

**Formula used:**

1) **Perimeter** = 4 × side (a)

2) **Area** = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

3) a² = (d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8a1a654d398b899e59e55d4ecc5f8eaee53219713c42bddce8ac771fe7fc0f51.png]

questions.question: The perimeter of a parallelogram is 48 cm. If the height of the parallelogram is 6 cm and the length of the adjacent side is 8 cm, find its area.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Sum of adjacent sides = **Perimeter** ÷ 2 = 48 ÷ 2 = 24 cm.

Base of the parallelogram = 24 − 8 = 16 cm.

**Area** = Base × Height = 16 × 6 = 96 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 96 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **Perimeter** of parallelogram = 48 cm

⇒ Length of one **adjacent side** (b) = 8 cm

⇒ **Height** (h) of the parallelogram = 6 cm

**Formula used:**

⇒ Perimeter = 2 × (Side₁ + Side₂)

⇒ Area = **Base** × **Height**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3afbec8c23573d2d29d13f48ddab286acb88782c07749c12adccadb17d97f34c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 48 = 2 × (Base + 8)

⇒ 24 = Base + 8

⇒ **Base** = 24 − 8 = 16 cm

⇒ **Area** = 16 × 6

⇒ **Area** = 96 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 96 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Area of Parallelogram

The area can be calculated as Area = a × b × sin(θ), where a and b are adjacent sides and θ is the angle between them.

Height and Side Relationship

In a parallelogram, the product of a side and its corresponding altitude is constant: Area = Base₁ × Height₁ = Base₂ × Height₂.

Properties of Parallelogram

Opposite sides are equal and parallel, and diagonals bisect each other.</p

questions.question: The ratio of the perimeter to the length of a rectangle is 5 : 2. If the area of the rectangle is 16 cm², then find the breadth of the rectangle (in cm).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Perimeter** to **Length** is 5 : 2 ⇒ 2(L + B) : L = 5 : 2.

Solving for relationship: 4L + 4B = 5L ⇒ **L = 4B**.

**Area** = L × B = (4B) × B = 4B² = 16 cm².

B² = 4 ⇒ **B = 2 cm**.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **Perimeter** (P) to **Length** (L) = 5 : 2

**Area** of the **Rectangle** = 16 cm²

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter (P) = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

Area (A) = Length × Breadth

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/61beaa75a9b46016abe878364ac3d5cdac8c0820a00615b30cff06b156115221.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ P / L = 5 / 2

⇒ 2(L + B) / L = 5 / 2

⇒ 4(L + B) = 5L

⇒ 4L + 4B = 5L

⇒ L = 4B

⇒ Area = L × B = 16

⇒ (4B) × B = 16

⇒ 4B² = 16

⇒ B² = 4

⇒ B = √4 = 2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 2 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of a Rectangle

The total boundary length of a rectangle is given by the formula P = 2 × (l + b), where l is length and b is breadth.

Area of a Rectangle

The total space occupied by a rectangle in a 2D plane is Area = Length × Breadth.

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The distance between opposite vertices is calculated using Pythagoras theorem: d = √(l² + b²).</p

**Formula used:**

Pythagoras Theorem:

Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

In an isosceles triangle if a perpendicular is drawn from a vertices to its opposite side then it will bisect the side into two equal parts 

**Calculation:**

AD perpendicular to BC

So, ΔADB is right angle triangle

Let AB = AC be x and BD be y

BD = DC (AD will bisect BC)

Now,

x + x + y + y = 50

⇒ x + y = 25 

⇒ x = 25 - y

From ΔABD

x² = y² + 5²

⇒ (25 - y)² = y² + 5²

⇒ 625 - 50y + y² = y² + 25

⇒ 50y = 625 - 25

⇒ 50y = 600

⇒ y = 600/50 

⇒ y = 12

⇒ BD = 12

Now,

BC = 2 × BD [∵ In isosceles triangle, altitude and median are same]

2BC = 24 × 2 = 48 cm

**∴ Twice the length of BC (in cm) is 48.**

questions.question: In an isosceles triangle ABC with AB = AC and AD is perpendicular to BC, if AD = 6 cm and the perimeter of ΔABC is 36 cm, then the area of ΔABC is:

So, AB² = AD² + BD²

⇒ a² = 6² + (b/2)²

⇒ a2 = 36 + b²/4

⇒ a2 - b2/4 = 36 

⇒ 4a2 - b2 = 36 × 4

⇒ (2a + b) (2a - b) = 144

Putting the value of (2a + b) from equation (1),

⇒ 36 × (2a - b) = 144

⇒ 2a - b = 4

Putting the value of b from equation (2),

⇒ 2 × (36 - b)/2 - b = 4

⇒ (36 - b) - b = 4

⇒ 36 - 2b = 4

⇒ 2b = 36 - 4 

⇒ b = 32/2 = 16 cm

∴ Area of triangle ABC is 48 cm2

questions.question: The lengths of the three sides of a triangle are given as 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. The ratio of their corresponding altitudes to the opposite vertices will be:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of altitudes of a triangle is always inversely proportional to the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Ratio of the given sides = 3 ∶ 4 ∶ 5

Ratio of their corresponding altitudes = 1/3 ∶ 1/4 ∶ 1/5

Multiplying by the LCM of (3, 4, 5) which is 60:

Ratio of altitudes = 20 ∶ 15 ∶ 12

**∴ The correct answer is 20 ∶ 15 ∶ 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/08e493ceb26d1cecf5ff24815ed689421e4dec774f95a6a6ae86e796bc93045a.png] 

**Given:**

Sides of the triangle, a = 3 cm, b = 4 cm, and c = 5 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Area of a triangle = 1/2 × base × height

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the corresponding altitudes to the given sides be h₁, h₂, and h₃.

⇒ Since 3² + 4² = 5², the given sides form a right-angled triangle.

⇒ Area of the triangle = 1/2 × 3 × 4 = 6 cm²

⇒ Altitude corresponding to side 3 cm: 1/2 × 3 × h₁ = 6 ⇒ h₁ = 4 cm

⇒ Altitude corresponding to side 4 cm: 1/2 × 4 × h₂ = 6 ⇒ h₂ = 3 cm

⇒ Altitude corresponding to side 5 cm: 1/2 × 5 × h₃ = 6 ⇒ h₃ = 12/5 = 2.4 cm

⇒ Ratio of altitudes = h₁ ∶ h₂ ∶ h₃ = 4 ∶ 3 ∶ 2.4

⇒ Multiply the ratio by 10 to remove the decimal: 40 ∶ 30 ∶ 24

⇒ Divide the terms by 2 to get the simplest integer form: 20 ∶ 15 ∶ 12

**∴ The correct answer is 20 ∶ 15 ∶ 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation Between Sides and Altitudes

Since the area of a given triangle is constant, an altitude is strictly inversely proportional to its corresponding base length. Therefore, a × hₐ = b × hb = c × h꜀.

Heron's Formula

The area of any scalene triangle can also be calculated universally using its side lengths: Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)], where s is the semi-perimeter given by (a+b+c)/2.

Pythagorean Triplet

A set of three positive integers that satisfy a² + b² = c² is known as a Pythagorean triplet. A triangle constructed with these specific side lengths is always right-angled at the vertex opposite to the longest side.

Circumference = 15 × 15 = 225 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 225 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of arc (l) = 15 cm

Angle subtended at the centre (θ) = 24°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a8f42db93cf91cbfad75b638fd0649cbc68de09360c22a4771aee208e3c189a8.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Length of an arc = (θ ÷ 360°) × Circumference

**Calculations:**

⇒ 15 = (24° ÷ 360°) × Circumference

⇒ 15 = (1 ÷ 15) × Circumference

⇒ Circumference = 15 × 15

⇒ Circumference = 225 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 225 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Sector

The area of a sector of a circle with radius r and central angle θ is given by Area = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr².

Circumference of a Circle

The total boundary length of a circle is calculated as C = 2πr or C = πd, which corresponds to the full 360° arc.

Radian Measure

When measuring angles in radians, the formula for arc length is simplified to l = r × θ. A complete circle is 2π radians.
</p

questions.question: The area of the sector of a circle is 128 cm². If the length of the arc of that sector is 64 cm, then find the radius of the circle.
questions.solution:
Given:

Area of the sector of a circle = 128 cm²

Length of the arc = 64 cm

Formula Used:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/99a765049b2690f787986d3a1bdf24d43c351a50867b80265632194aa65496fc.png] 

Area = (lr)/(2)

Calculations:

According to the formula,

⇒ Area = (lr)/(2)

⇒ 128 = (64 times r)/(2)

⇒ r = 2 x 2 = 4 cm

⇒ **Hence, The radius of the circle is 4 cm**
